Adding Bayesian-smoothed per-video and per-author long_view rate as bucketed FM features, plus averaging within-user fractional ranks across 3 seeds, will raise validation primary by approximately +0.002 over the baseline FM
mechanism: Smoothed CTR provides a calibrated prior for each video/author's quality that is regularized for sparse IDs, encoding signal beyond the raw embedding. Rank averaging across seeds reduces variance in the ordinal scores that GAUC and nDCG@5 measure — because the metric only reads ordering, rank-space averaging is more direct than score-space averaging. Together these two effects compose additively.

evidence.task_structure: Within-user ranking over ~5 candidates. A video's historical long_view rate computed from strictly prior training rows varies across a user's candidate videos and provides signal orthogonal to the video ID embedding for sparse IDs. Rank averaging reduces seed-specific ordering noise in a ~5-item list.

evidence.literature: No directly relevant papers found in search this iteration.

Then train 3 FM instances with seeds 0,1,2, convert each model's scores to per-user fractional ranks, and average the ranks as the final score.

risks.overfitting: Smoothing (Bayesian prior toward global mean) prevents overfitting on rare videos/authors; ensembling further reduces variance
risks.runtime: 3 FM models at ~40s each = ~2 minutes total, well within 25 minute limit

hypothesis: Adding a bucketed feature encoding how the candidate video's duration compares to this user's historical duration preference (computed from train-only long_view=1 interactions) will improve within-user ranking by providing a signal that varies across a user's impression list.
mechanism: The metric is within-user ordering. User-constant features cancel. A ratio of candidate_duration / user_preferred_duration varies across impressions for the same user because different candidates have different durations. Users who historically engaged with short videos will rank short candidates higher, and vice versa. This creates a genuine cross-user-video interaction term that the FM can leverage via its pairwise embedding dot products.

evidence.task_structure: Median 35 training interactions per validation user (p10=6). Duration varies substantially across videos (P10=13s, P50=72s, P90=236s). Long_view rate varies by duration. With 98.4% of validation users having training history, this feature is well-covered.
evidence.previous_experiments: Node 2 established that smoothed CTR buckets give ~0.0008 gain. The coverage analysis shows 98.4% of validation users have training history. The established findings note that interaction features failed due to overfitting in prior runs, but those were complex features; this is a simple ratio with heavy smoothing.
evidence.literature: No search this iteration — mechanism is clear from task structure and metric definitions.

proposed_change: Compute per-user mean duration_ms of training rows where long_view=1 (smoothed toward global mean with prior_strength=20). For each impression row, compute ratio = candidate_duration / user_duration_preference, bucket into 10 quantile-based bins. Add this as an extra FM feature column alongside the existing smoothed CTR buckets.
expected_result: Gain of 0.002-0.005 on validation primary. If it fails to exceed noise floor, the mechanism (duration preference) may be too noisy or the FM may not capture this interaction well.
falsification_condition: If val_primary improves by less than 0.002 over node 2's 0.6036, the feature does not contribute meaningful signal in this model architecture.

risks.leakage: None — user's duration preference is computed from strictly past (training) rows only. Candidate duration_ms is known before watching. The ratio uses only pre-impression information.
risks.overfitting: Low — the feature is smoothed toward the global mean and bucketed into only 10 bins. Users with few training impressions of long_view=1 will fall close to the global mean bucket, which is correct behavior.
risks.runtime: Negligible — just adds one feature column computation loop. Training time unchanged.

candidates_considered: LightGBM with continuous duration and other features — allows non-linear combinations but changes model family entirely; uncertain effect size
Per-user duration preference interaction: user's mean duration of long_view=1 videos in training, divided by candidate duration, bucketed — a clean interaction term that varies across the user's list
Pairwise ranking loss instead of pointwise BCE — better aligned with nDCG/GAUC but requires custom training code and uncertain convergence behavior
reflection: Node 2 achieved +0.0020 with smoothed CTR features + 3-seed rank ensemble. That is a real but modest gain. The remaining signal must come from interaction terms that vary across a user's impression list. User-side features alone cancel out within-user ranking, but a feature like 'candidate duration relative to this user's historical preference' varies across the candidates shown to one user and is legitimate.

hypothesis: A LightGBM model trained with LambdaRank objective, using user/video/author label-encoded categoricals plus continuous Bayesian-smoothed video and author CTR features, will outperform the FM baseline because it directly optimizes NDCG and can capture non-linear feature interactions
mechanism: LambdaRank computes gradients that directly optimize NDCG; grouping by user at training time matches the evaluation structure (within-user ranking); tree splits can capture threshold effects and interactions that FM's linear+pairwise-interaction structure cannot represent; continuous CTR features avoid quantization loss from bucketing

evidence.task_structure: The evaluation is purely within-user ranking over ~5 impressions; LambdaRank with user-level groups trains exactly for this objective; the 1.14M training rows with ~44 rows/user provide enough group-level signal for gradient boosting
evidence.previous_experiments: Node 2 showed smoothed video/author CTR features help; LightGBM can use these as continuous values without bucketing, potentially extracting more signal from them
evidence.literature: No new search conducted; existing papers on LambdaMART (W2912255075) confirm pairwise/listwise objectives improve ranking over pointwise losses

proposed_change: Replace FM with LightGBM LambdaRank model. Features: label-encoded user_id, video_id, author_id, tab, dur_bucket (from encode()), plus continuous smoothed video CTR and author CTR from training data. Group training rows by user_id for LambdaRank. Use rank ensemble over 3 seeds with different random states for tree feature subsampling.
expected_result: VAL_PRIMARY in range 0.61-0.63, a gain of +0.005 to +0.02 over the FM baseline of 0.6036
falsification_condition: If VAL_PRIMARY <= 0.6016 (baseline) or the gain is less than 0.002 above node 2's 0.6036, the hypothesis is wrong — either LambdaRank does not help at this scale/group-size or the tree model overfits

risks.leakage: Smoothed CTR computed from training rows only, strictly before validation rows — no leakage
risks.overfitting: With ~26K users and ~44 rows/user in training, tree model could overfit user IDs; mitigated by not using raw user_id as a feature (high cardinality), or using low max_depth and regularization
risks.runtime: LightGBM is fast; 1.14M rows with ~26K groups should train in under 2 minutes

candidates_considered: Increase FM ensemble from 3 to 5 seeds: marginal gain expected (~+0.0005), high runtime cost (15+ model trainings per evaluation), not worth the iteration budget
LightGBM LambdaRank with continuous smoothed CTR features: directly optimizes NDCG, handles continuous inputs natively, can capture non-linear interactions FM cannot, potentially large gain
Pairwise BPR loss on FM: aligns objective with ranking metric but requires substantial code change while staying in same model family with limited additional capacity
reflection: Node 3 regressed by adding a per-user duration preference feature that was constant within each user's list, confirming the established finding that per-user aggregates with no within-user variation are useless. Node 2 remains best at 0.6036 using FM + smoothed CTR buckets + 3-seed rank ensemble. The next logical move is to try a fundamentally different model family rather than adding more features to FM.

hypothesis: Replacing the pointwise BCE loss in the FM with a pairwise BPR loss (sampling user-level positive/negative pairs) will improve GAUC and nDCG@5 because the training objective directly optimizes within-user relative ordering, matching the evaluation metric structure
mechanism: GAUC and nDCG@5 both measure within-user ranking quality. Pointwise BCE treats each row independently, oblivious to the relative ordering of items shown to the same user. BPR explicitly samples pairs (pos_item, neg_item) for each user and applies log-sigmoid loss on score(pos) - score(neg), directly pushing positives above negatives within each user. With ~44 rows/user in training, there are many within-user pairs to learn from. This alignment between training loss and evaluation objective should improve generalization to the 5-impression evaluation setting.

evidence.task_structure: The metric is entirely within-user (GAUC averages per-user AUC; nDCG@5 ranks within each user's impression list). With ~44 training impressions per user and ~3.78 mean long_view rate, each user has ~17 positives and ~27 negatives, giving ~459 valid pairs per user — ample signal for pairwise training.
evidence.previous_experiments: Node 2 established the FM backbone is effective (0.6036). Nodes 3 and 4 showed that adding complexity via features or model changes risks regression. BPR keeps the same FM architecture and only changes the loss, which is a minimal surgical change.
evidence.literature: [W2798881875] BPR with improved sampling demonstrates that pairwise ranking loss substantially outperforms pointwise alternatives on implicit feedback data, directly supporting this mechanism. [W2963655167] VBPR applies BPR to visual FM, confirming FM+BPR combination works well.

proposed_change: Implement BPR pairwise training loop on top of the FM from node 2 (same smoothed CTR features, same 3-seed rank ensemble). For each mini-batch: sample random (user, pos_item, neg_item) triples from training data, compute score(pos) - score(neg) using FM logits, apply -log(sigmoid(diff)) as the loss, and backprop. Keep Adam optimizer. Early stop on validation primary with patience 4.
expected_result: +0.003 to +0.005 improvement in validation primary over node 2 (0.6036), primarily from GAUC improvement since BPR directly optimizes AUC
falsification_condition: If validation primary stays within 0.002 of node 2 (i.e., below 0.6056), the hypothesis is falsified — the pairwise loss either failed to converge or the gain is inside the noise floor

risks.leakage: None — BPR only uses item labels and user groupings from the same training rows, no future information
risks.overfitting: BPR can overfit on users with few interactions. Mitigated by L2 regularization inherited from FM and early stopping on validation. Training has ~44 rows/user so overfitting risk is moderate.
risks.runtime: BPR sampling per batch is O(batch_size) and comparable to BCE. 3 seeds × ~10 epochs should stay well under 10 minutes, similar to node 2.

candidates_considered: BPR pairwise loss for FM: sample (user, pos, neg) pairs within each user and optimize log-sigmoid of score difference — directly trains the ranking objective GAUC measures, expected +0.003-0.005
Larger ensemble (5 seeds instead of 3): known to give +0.0016 from established findings but costs 5x training time and adds ~15 reruns, may be below the readable threshold given iteration cost
Temperature/sharpening post-processing: apply power transform to ensemble ranks to sharpen within-user differences — very cheap but expected effect <0.002, likely noise
reflection: Node 4 (LightGBM LambdaRank) regressed significantly (-0.0057). The main cause is that LambdaRank on sparse categorical features (especially user_id with ~26k distinct values) doesn't generalize as well as the FM's embedding-based approach. The FM's shared embedding space lets it generalize across users/items. Node 2 remains the best at 0.6036 with smoothed CTR buckets + 3-seed rank ensemble. The established findings show FM is the right backbone; the question is how to squeeze more from it.
